approvedContract.comprehensionObjective: Recognize a timekeeper can assist an east–west navigation problem.
approvedContract.continuityRequirements: Reference and ship identities persist; every later angle is measured from the same reference.
approvedContract.disclosureRequirements: Conceptual scene, not historical voyage footage; longitude is angular east–west position.
approvedContract.mustCommunicate: A ship and ordinary TIME indication supply the information gap; establish a known reference meridian and an unresolved ship meridian.
approvedContract.mustNotImply: No complete position fix, longitude pointer on the clock, latitude value or GPS behavior.

beats.prohibition: No geographic coordinate appears on its dial. Ship is an explanatory symbol, not an H4 trial reconstruction.
beats.proposedRealization: A watch-shaped reference-time object sits beside a small abstract hull on a shallow-relief ocean field. The hook is spoken immediately; no ticking intro.

approvedContract.comprehensionObjective: Understand the timekeeper carries time tied to somewhere known.
approvedContract.continuityRequirements: Same reference origin and carried timekeeper persist through comparison and payoff.
approvedContract.disclosureRequirements: Reference time is mean solar time; displayed value is corrected for known clock error, with date/day ambiguity resolved.
approvedContract.mustCommunicate: Separate the reference location from the ship; carried reference reading stays tied to that location rather than being reset to local time.
approvedContract.mustNotImply: Not a clock remotely receiving an eighteenth-century live signal; not universal historical Greenwich.

beats.prohibition: Reference is a chosen meridian, not an assertion of universal historical Greenwich usage. No clock reset.
beats.proposedRealization: Keep the same carried clock object visible; a tethered reference-meridian marker on the globe identifies the chosen known location. Label REFERENCE TIME.

approvedContract.comprehensionObjective: Understand observation supplies local time and the solar observation must be corrected to a comparable basis.
approvedContract.continuityRequirements: Distinguish the carried reference reading from the local observation throughout; local readout is a derived display, not a second independent historical marine clock.
approvedContract.disclosureRequirements: Corrected to match means converting apparent solar time to mean solar time with the equation of time, not a time-zone change or resetting the ship clock. No date-specific correction number or new noon geometry is asserted.
approvedContract.mustCommunicate: Sun-derived APPARENT SOLAR TIME is converted to LOCAL MEAN SOLAR TIME before the example. Required factual disclosure: BOTH MEAN SOLAR TIME.
approvedContract.mustNotImply: Do not compare raw sundial/noon observation with uncorrected mean-clock time. Do not make a sundial or second carried clock magically give local time.

beats.prohibition: Correction modifies the derived local reading, never reference-clock hands. This is a conceptual observation, not a prescribed sextant operation or historical sundial aboard the ship.
beats.proposedRealization: A Sun marker and horizon/observation glyph yield an OBSERVED SOLAR TIME card. A separate correction-to-mean-time step produces LOCAL MEAN TIME beside the untouched reference reading. BOTH MEAN SOLAR TIME is legible.

approvedContract.comprehensionObjective: Understand this is a simultaneous spatial comparison rather than a ship journey lasting two hours.
approvedContract.continuityRequirements: Shared instant is retained in the numerical example; neither reading advances alone.
approvedContract.disclosureRequirements: Illustrative comparison, not claimed measured voyage data.
approvedContract.mustCommunicate: Lock both corrected readings to ONE INSTANT; required disclosure SAME INSTANT.
approvedContract.mustNotImply: No elapsed-voyage inference from the difference; no comparison of different dates without resolving day branch.

beats.prohibition: No elapsed-voyage timer or time-zone conversion; two readings are simultaneous, not two successive moments.
beats.proposedRealization: Both readings settle in one held comparison frame with SAME INSTANT and stable reference/local labels. Freeze the values before calculating.

approvedContract.comprehensionObjective: Understand why different meridians have different local solar times and why the time gap maps to an angle.
approvedContract.continuityRequirements: Keep viewing orientation and east direction unambiguous;15° marks longitude angle, not latitude or orbital angle.
approvedContract.disclosureRequirements: SCHEMATIC / SOLAR-TIME RELATIONSHIP. Geometry may express reviewed angles; the physical scene is not a precision astronomical simulation.
approvedContract.mustCommunicate: Relate Sun/Earth meridians to a labeled15° angle per1h of consistent solar-time difference.
approvedContract.mustNotImply: No exact360° stellar-relative rotation in24SIhours; no civil-zone boundaries or universal distance per degree.

beats.prohibition: Mean-solar explanatory conversion; no sidereal 23h56m label, clockwork literal linkage or universal distance conversion.
beats.proposedRealization: Use a north-pole plan view of the globe with meridian rays: a one-hour interval maps to a labeled 15° wedge. Preserve an east arrow and globe orientation.

approvedContract.comprehensionObjective: Understand12:00 reference and14:00 local are simultaneous comparable readings.
approvedContract.continuityRequirements: Maintain same reference origin, same instant and corrected-time basis from earlier beats.
approvedContract.disclosureRequirements: These are illustrative mean times; no actual date, historical voyage or measured clock error is introduced.
approvedContract.mustCommunicate: Show12:00 reference and14:00 local with BOTH MEAN SOLAR TIME / SAME INSTANT / ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE; identify two in the afternoon as14:00.
approvedContract.mustNotImply: Do not call12:00 apparent local noon or mark14:00 as noon; no unrestricted ordinary wall-clock time-zone comparison.

beats.prohibition: 14:00 is an explanatory notation on a label, not painted onto a historical watch or meant as zone/civil time.
beats.proposedRealization: Two equal-status explanatory readout cards show REFERENCE 12:00 and LOCAL 14:00 at one frozen instant; keep mean-time basis legible.

approvedContract.comprehensionObjective: Understand local time ahead corresponds to east, and2×15° gives30°.
approvedContract.continuityRequirements: Same ship/reference meridians; eastward angular displacement is consistent with the earlier view and time relation.
approvedContract.disclosureRequirements: Illustrative calculation, not a claim of perfect navigation or exact historical position.
approvedContract.mustCommunicate: Convert +2h local-minus-reference into +30° EAST OF THE REFERENCE; required factual label30°E RELATIVE TO REFERENCE.
approvedContract.mustNotImply: Never reverse east/west, draw30° latitude, present complete geographic position or equate30° with a universal distance.

beats.prohibition: Advance angular comparison, not the ship sailing along an elapsed-time route. No precise pin or latitude implied.
beats.proposedRealization: Local minus reference resolves to +2 HOURS; its interval extends to a 30° arc east of the reference meridian. Hold 30° EAST. Reference ray stays fixed; local ray is 30° counterclockwise in the north-pole view, explicitly labeled EAST.

approvedContract.comprehensionObjective: Recognize Harrison’s important contribution without replacing the mechanism with biography.
approvedContract.continuityRequirements: Historical device identity remains distinct from generic illustrative time readouts; do not imply the12:00/14:00 example is H4’s recorded trial.
approvedContract.disclosureRequirements: H4 object identity is an editorial factual requirement, not a choice of medium. Any future reconstruction or collection photograph requires accuracy/rights review; no media selected.
approvedContract.mustCommunicate: Identify H4 as a large LONGITUDE WATCH; associate it with John Harrison and qualified sea-going timekeeping demonstration.
approvedContract.mustNotImply: No sole invention of longitude, first-ever universal timekeeper, instant fleet adoption, full-prize claim, later boxed chronometer substituted forH4, or detailed unsupported mechanism.

beats.prohibition: Not a boxed gimballed later chronometer. No invented inner mechanism, archival footage, winner/prize title or biographical hero montage.
beats.proposedRealization: Brief original H4 watch study in the same object theatre, identified H4 · EXPLANATORY RECONSTRUCTION. Use large watch silhouette, silver case and enamel face; reserve exact detailing pending source/rights check.

approvedContract.comprehensionObjective: Understand marine clocks did not erase other longitude approaches.
approvedContract.continuityRequirements: This complements the local solar observation already needed; other astronomical methods are distinct from that local-time observation.
approvedContract.disclosureRequirements: A generic indication of astronomy is sufficient; detailed lunar geometry, tables or figures would add claims and require upstream review.
approvedContract.mustCommunicate: Preserve a complementary astronomical-method indication alongside the timekeeper concept.
approvedContract.mustNotImply: Do not show astronomy disappearing, lunar distances mandatory for every clock-based fix, or all ships instantly replacing dead reckoning.

beats.prohibition: Other methods are complementary, not crossed out, obsolete or instantaneously replaced. No added named-method claim beyond approved evidence.
beats.proposedRealization: Watch and astronomical observation/table symbols remain present side by side; the conceptual observation can continue with the watch present.

approvedContract.comprehensionObjective: Leave the viewer with the correct causal system.
approvedContract.continuityRequirements: Return to the existing comparison and angular result; do not introduce another location, instrument or factual relationship.
approvedContract.disclosureRequirements: Preserve relative reference, corrected mean-time basis, simultaneous readings and illustrative status in any final factual presentation.
approvedContract.mustCommunicate: Resolve REFERENCE TIME + LOCAL OBSERVATION/TIME + COMPARISON/CALCULATION → LONGITUDE, using the same corrected example and reference.
approvedContract.mustNotImply: Clock time is not a position display; longitude alone does not establish latitude or complete position; not a navigation tutorial guaranteeing accuracy.

beats.prohibition: Output is longitude only, not complete geographic position. No GPS-style location lock or CTA competing with the explanation.
beats.proposedRealization: Return to the original watch and ship arrangement, now retaining the reference-time card, observation card, comparison and a meridian at 30° east of the reference. Final three roles stay distinct.

finalSafeguards: H4 IS A LARGE LONGITUDE WATCH
